svg.title: gov-tla B4 — Government.tla: the authority graph — who creates, fills, directs and removes whom, and which claims about it are proved, checked, sampled or refuted
svg.desc: A directed, labelled multigraph over the People, the States, the Constitution, the three branches, the Vice President, and the agencies and inferior courts Congress creates. Every act fires one edge, by its holder; statutes, amendments and courts reshape the graph. Each reachability claim is stated twice: a local form, proved, and a global form over Reach, checked by TLC and not proved. The liveness property UnconstitutionalEdgesAreStruck is checked, not proved, and two claims of the module's first version are refuted by TLC. This models the text's procedure; it is an exercise, not law (README, opening).

svg.text: Checked means TLC explored every reachable state at the constants in the row list. Proved means TLAPS discharged every obligation for every value of the constants the module's named assumptions admit. Sampled means random simulation found no error, and is never cited as a check. Refuted means TLC found a counterexample to a claim the model was expected to satisfy. "None of these is a claim about law or practice" (README § How the specs are written and checked).

text.tspan: The grant layer: where authority comes from, read from

svg.text: The other three modules model what each branch does. This one models how authority runs between them: a directed, labelled multigraph over the People, the States, the Constitution, the three branches, the Vice President, and the agencies and inferior courts Congress creates. Edges come in two layers: Grant — where authority comes from: Power (vesting clauses, enabling acts), Select (elections, nomination, consent), Amend (Articles V, VII). Control — one holder acting on another's exercise of power: veto, override, purse, impeachment, removal,
review, pardon. (README § Government.tla.) One arrow per pair of nodes, labelled with each kind and label; the agency's conditional edges carry the enabling act's option (x, r, v).

Each cell lists the labels of the edges from the holder onto the target. Bold numbers count the edges between two branches. Red: the five Challengeable edges, those a
An agency's edges are drawn by its enabling act (AgencyEdges(a, x, r, v)); Direct only if it has executive power (x), one removal edge by r. A later bill (EdgesAfter) adds
Every branch has a control edge onto each other branch: every off-diagonal cell among the three branches is filled, and no statute joins two branches.
So the control layer among the branches is cyclic. That global form is over Reach: checked, not proved.

Fire(e) is OnGraph(e) /\ Held(e): the edge is in the graph and its holder is seated (Active), unless M_OFFEDGE or M_INACTIVE removes the check; an act that strayed is recorded in stray. IsInert labels: Appropriate, AdviseTreaties, DeclareWar, Pardon, Direct, AppointInferior, Jurisdiction, Appeal, LegislativeVeto, DiminishPay, DecideInability, DeclareInability, PresideTrial, PresideSenate, and Review onto anything but Congress, Nominate and Consent onto the Judiciary.

text.tspan: The README's claims table, every row and column, with the theorem and the TLC rows behind each name

svg.text: The graph claims are about reachability, which no single action decides. Each claim is therefore stated twice: a local form, which one action could break and that action's guard decides, proved; the global form, kept under its old name and checked by TLC, which follows from the local forms beside it. (README § Government.tla.)

ABSTRACTED: vote counts (see the other modules), persons, State governments' internal structure, the Youngstown framework, standing (any statutory edge whose label is in

Rights. Two later amendments that change the graph's shape are modelled: XVII (the Senate chosen by the People) and XXV (the President nominates a Vice President whom

svg.text: A witness is existential: a run that reaches the state is evidence that it is reachable at those constants, and no proof is attempted (README § What is not proved). TLC records no distinct-state count for a violated temporal property. The pairing of rows with the README's bullets is the diagram's.

text.tspan: A claim TLC refuted: the grant layer of 1789 is not acyclic once XXV gives the President a nomination

svg.text: Government.tla first folded the Vice President into the Executive. It claimed that, with the People and the States set aside, the grant layer is acyclic and runs strictly down the chain Constitution →
Congress → Executive → Judiciary. With the Vice President as a node of its own, TLC refutes both claims in two steps:
r-o-none-acyclic, Mut = "none", o: COUNTEREXAMPLE, 26 distinct states, as expected.
r-o-none-chain, Mut = "none", o: COUNTEREXAMPLE, 26 distinct states, as expected.

text.tspan: What it is, and what was kept

svg.text: Section 2 of the Twenty-fifth Amendment lets the President nominate a Vice President, and the Vice President may succeed the President. So Executive → Vice President → Executive is a cycle of
authority that never passes through the People or the States. It is how Gerald Ford became President in 1974, nominated by Nixon in 1973 and confirmed by Congress, and how Ford then chose
Nelson Rockefeller. Before XXV the claims hold: a vacant Vice Presidency simply stayed vacant.
The original properties are kept, unchanged, as GrantCyclesPassThroughPeopleOrStates and GrantFollowsChain. The rows r-o-none-acyclic and r-o-none-chain expect, and get, a
counterexample under Mut = "none". They replace Government_strict.cfg.
Module header: REFUTED CLAIMS, kept unchanged: GrantCyclesPassThroughPeopleOrStates and GrantFollowsChain. Both held while the Vice President was folded into the Executive; with the
VP as a node TLC refutes both under Mut = "none" in two steps (propose XXV, ratify it). See the comment at their definitions.

What holds instead is drawn above: GrantFollowsChainExceptXXV (proved) and GrantCyclesPassThroughPeopleStatesOrVP (checked), which set the Vice Presidency aside too, and OnlyGrantCycleIsXXV (checked): the loop is the only inner grant cycle, present exactly under XXV.
Government.tla models the same session with the same name (inSession, commented "is Congress sitting?"). There, Pass (line 646) and Override (line 698) both require it,
as do Veto, PocketVeto and Lapse, the last through CanReturn.
The modules disagree. In Government.tla an adjourned Congress cannot pass a bill or override a veto. In Constitution.tla it can. Neither header says so.
Government's two guards are untested. The method makes every check a guard that one mutation removes, and requires that removal to break a property. No mutation
removes inSession from Pass or Override, and no property says passage happens only in session. TLC has never been shown that either guard changes anything. This was

text.tspan: Checked by the diagram, and its reading

svg.text: Checked at build time: Government.tla line 646 (in Pass) and line 698 (in Override) are /\ inSession, as § 5 says.
The diagram's reading: no mutation in the header's list removes either guard, so no column of the matrix above tests them.
